transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
Russia launched a mass overnight attack on Ukraine using ballistic missiles,
killing at least two people.
NPR's Joanna Kikisas reports from Kyiv.
In Kyiv, Russian ballistic missiles also hit transportation and medical facilities.
The explosions were heard clearly from NPR's bureau.
Writing on social media, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky
noted that this attack comes after Russia agreed to restart U.S.-led talks to end the war.
Speaking to reporters via voice message on Wednesday night, Zelensky said he is pushing for peace.
Not everything depends on us, he says.
We will support a proposal for a ceasefire to lead to the end of the war,
as well as an energy ceasefire, or any kind of ceasefire for that matter.
President Trump has repeatedly accused Zelensky of not wanting to make a deal to end the war.
Joanna Kikisas, NPR News, Kyiv.
The International Monetary Fund says the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran has led to economic shocks across the mid-East.
NPR's Ea Betray reports oil exporting countries are seeing double-digit contractions to their economies.
A new report by the IMF says disruptions to energy production, shipping, tourism and trade this year
have delivered substantial shocks to countries in the Gulf,
even as higher oil prices offset some of these losses for energy exporters.
The international lender says Iraq, Kuwait and Qatar are all expected to experience contractions of around 16 percent to their economies this year.
The economies of Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates are also in recession this year.
The IMF says if the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran continues and energy supply disruptions persist,
the price of oil will average $130 a barrel in 2027.
Ea Betray, NPR News, Dubai.
President Trump heads to Iowa today to continue campaigning for GOP candidates ahead of the midterms.
These are now less than two weeks away.
The president was in South Carolina last night attending a rally for GOP Senator Darlene Graham,
the sister of the late Senator Lindsey Graham,
and Piers Franco-Odonas has mourned.
President Trump urged the very enthusiastic crowd at Clemson University to show up at the polls
to help elect Darlene Graham and other Republicans.
Trump spoke of Graham carrying on the legacy of her brother, who was a close ally to the president.
I asked Darlene to run, and after a little thought, because it's a very big decision, it really is,
and she said yes, and I was very happy about it.
Graham is in a surprisingly tight race for such a red state running against Democrat Annie Andrews,
but Trump has struggled politically as the war in Iran has dragged on, and gas prices have surged.
NPR's Franco-Odonas reporting. This is NPR.
The National Hurricane Center says subtropical storm Josephine is still bringing significant coastal flooding
to parts of the eastern seaboard.
Forecasters say Josephine's top sustained winds are at 65 miles per hour.
It's just off Massachusetts.
The center says Josephine should move away from the U.S. in the next few days.
Shares and electric vehicle maker Tesla fell more than 3 percent in after-hours trading yesterday.
That's after the company reported flat revenue for the third quarter compared with the same quarter last year.
And Piers Willow Rubin reports.
Most of Tesla's money comes from selling cars, especially the Model 3 and the Model Y.
And those sales dropped during the quarter compared with the same period last year.
In a call with analysts, CEO Elon Musk didn't talk much about cars, though.
Instead, he focused on the kinds of technologies Tesla is investing a ton in,
like robotaxes and building humanoid robots.
While capital expenditures more than doubled from the same quarter last year,
they were down from the previous quarter.
Musk was also asked about his announcement on Tuesday's SpaceX earnings call
that the two companies had launched special committees to explore the possibility of merging.
But he said they weren't going to take more questions about it.
And he said talking about it was like "tap dancing through a minefield."
Willow Rubin, NPR News.
In the WNBA Finals, the Atlanta dream beat the Golden State Valkyries last night, '97 to '71, at home.
Atlanta has taken a two-games-to-one lead in the series.
You're listening to NPR.

topics.text: Russia launches mass overnight ballistic missile attack on Ukraine, killing at least two people
Zelensky says he backs ceasefire proposals as Russia agrees to restart U.S.-led peace talks
IMF report finds U.S.-Israeli war on Iran causing economic contractions across Gulf states
Trump campaigns in South Carolina for Senator Lindsey Graham's sister Darlene Graham ahead of midterms
Subtropical storm Josephine brings coastal flooding to eastern seaboard, now off Massachusetts
Tesla reports flat quarterly revenue as car sales drop; shares fall after hours
Atlanta Dream beat Golden State Valkyries 97-71, taking 2-1 lead in WNBA Finals
